newsitem.title: USA: US spot natgas prices stalled by moderate weather.
newsitem.headline: US spot natgas prices stalled by moderate weather.

text.p: U.S. spot natural gas prices were little changed again on Friday, as many buyers remained on the sidelines due to the moderate weather throughout most of the U.S. and lack of sharp movement on the futures side.
Louisiana Gulf Coast prices were on either side of unchanged in the high-$1.80s. Henry Hub was quoted in the high-$1.80s early and the low-$1.90s late.

Despite a brief cool spell expected this weekend in the Midwest and early next week in the Northeast, temperatures are forecast to climb to above-normal levels by the middle of next week, Weather Services Corp said.
In south Texas, prices gained about three cents as cooler temperatures were forecast for the region this weekend.
Permian gas prices were similarly up more than five cents to the $1.70-1.78 range, while southern California border prices also moved into the mid-$1.70s.
Traders blamed the uptick on the reemergence of buyers on the West Coast to balance end-of-the-month loads since current market values were about 80 cents under February indices.
March Permian prices were talked in the $1.50s.
Southern California Edison's 1,070 megawatt San Onofre 2 nuclear power unit is expected not to restart until early March.

In the Midcontinent, prices were stable to up slightly in the low-to-mid $1.70s in fairly light trade ahead of the weekend, still nearly 20 cents lower than week-ago levels. Demarcation gas for the weekend sold mostly in the mid-$1.70s, sources said.
Temperatures in the Midwest are expected to turn cooler over the weekend but then return to normal to above-normal levels by Wednesday.
In the East, New York city-gate prices slipped a couple of cents to the $2.10-2.15 range as the region anticipated temperatures about 20-30 degrees F above normal.
Appalachian prices were equally lower in the low-$2 area.
Ahead of Monday's expiry of NYMEX's March contract, cash and futures were for the most part in convergence.
Some traders speculated that the lack of weather-driven demand and the ample availability of storage supplies could lead to more softness in cash early next week.

American Gas Association reported Wednesday that U.S. gas inventories as of Feb 14 were down 147 bcf to 35 percent of capacity. In the East, stocks at 687 bcf were 233 bcf, or 51 percent above year-ago.
